product_overview: PAIMANA AI is a predictive analytics and early warning system for monitoring infrastructure projects. It combines project dashboards, searchable exploration, deep project analytics, and model benchmarking to help users identify risk, delays, and cost overruns early.
core_goals: Provide a centralized overview of infrastructure project performance and risk
Enable users to search, filter, and inspect projects efficiently
Deliver deep-dive project analytics including forecasts, milestones, and explainability
Surface early warning alerts for high-risk, delayed, or cost-overrunning projects
Compare model performance across statistical and machine learning approaches

features.name: Overview Dashboard
features.description: Shows high-level KPIs, risk distribution, sector breakdowns, and an early warning summary for infrastructure projects.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/projects/summary -> Receive 200 with KPI totals and overview metrics -> GET /api/v1/risk/distribution -> Receive 200 with risk distribution data -> GET /api/v1/alerts/summary -> Receive 200 with early warning summary
GET /api/v1/projects/summary with backend unavailable -> Receive 500 error and no dashboard metrics returned
GET /api/v1/risk/distribution with invalid query context -> Receive 400 error describing the issue

features.name: Project Explorer
features.description: Provides a searchable and filterable project directory with sector, state, risk tier, cost filters, sorting, and pagination.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/projects/filters -> Receive 200 with available filter options -> GET /api/v1/projects with valid filter and pagination parameters -> Receive 200 with matching project list and paging metadata
GET /api/v1/projects with unsupported filter values -> Receive 400 error explaining invalid filters
GET /api/v1/projects/filters -> Receive 200 with filters -> GET /api/v1/projects with overly restrictive criteria -> Receive 200 with an empty results set

features.name: Project Detail & Deep Dive
features.description: Displays a detailed project profile including progress curves, delay drivers, risk scoring, ML predictions, and SHAP explainability.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/projects/{id} with a valid project id -> Receive 200 with project profile and deep-dive data -> GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/predictions -> Receive 200 with forecast outputs -> GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/explainability -> Receive 200 with SHAP-based feature contributions -> GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/milestones -> Receive 200 with milestone timeline
GET /api/v1/projects/{id} with a nonexistent project id -> Receive 404 error indicating project not found
GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/predictions with missing or malformed id -> Receive 400 or 404 error depending on validation outcome

features.name: Early Warning Alerts
features.description: Surfaces real-time early warning alerts for high-risk projects, critical delay escalations, and cost overrun anomalies.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/alerts -> Receive 200 with active alerts sorted by severity and category -> POST /api/v1/alerts/acknowledge with a valid alert identifier -> Receive 200 confirming the alert was acknowledged
GET /api/v1/alerts -> Receive 200 with alert list -> POST /api/v1/alerts/acknowledge with an invalid alert identifier -> Receive 404 or 400 error indicating the alert cannot be acknowledged
GET /api/v1/alerts with no active warnings -> Receive 200 with an empty alert state and informational summary

features.name: Model Comparison & Analytics
features.description: Compares classical statistical models with advanced machine learning models and CUF ablation metrics.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/models/metrics -> Receive 200 with benchmark metrics for statistical and ML models -> GET /api/v1/models/ablation -> Receive 200 with CUF ablation results and comparative analysis
GET /api/v1/models/metrics -> Receive 200 with metrics -> GET /api/v1/models/ablation with unsupported parameters -> Receive 400 error describing invalid request
GET /api/v1/models/metrics when model outputs are unavailable -> Receive 500 error and no comparison data returned
